fatal_errors: The proposed Q235 ultrasonic surface treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention: an atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L followed by 2 h annealing, optimally at 550 °C.
The proposed saltwater and approximately 300 °C exposures do not match either the target 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical test or the 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion tests.
The mechanism omits the governing Al- and Cr-rich chemistry, coating barrier, BCC/FCC phase balance, sluggish diffusion, molten-salt penetration, and oxide-scale fluxing central to the target.

The cited evidence concerns grain-refined alloys and ultrasonic treatment of other alloy systems; it does not directly establish improved passivation of Q235 steel, especially at elevated temperature.
The experiment does not isolate grain size from ultrasonic-treatment confounders such as residual compressive stress, roughness, dislocation density, contamination, and work hardening.
explanation: The hypothesis is a scientifically conceivable alternative for room-temperature corrosion of grain-refined steel, and its treated-versus-untreated design includes useful electrochemical and surface measurements. It nevertheless has little agreement with the hidden target's material, coating process, annealing schedule, environments, and hot-corrosion outcomes. Its evidence supports only the general links between grain refinement, oxidation nucleation, and ultrasonic deformation in other alloys. Q235 does not ordinarily form the same stable Al/Cr-rich passive layers as the target HEA coating, so transfer of the passivation mechanism is weak. The elevated-temperature condition is also underspecified and may not involve an electrolyte or corrosion regime comparable to the target. A stronger causal test would independently vary grain size while matching roughness and residual stress, characterize the film before and during exposure, and show that corrosion resistance tracks grain refinement rather than those correlated treatment effects. The arbitrary greater-than-20% threshold is not itself a mechanistically decisive falsification criterion.
